ENST 202.title: Climate Emergency
ENST 202.description: Science, impacts, and parallel crises of the climate emergency; decarbonization challenge and measuring progress towards emission targets; strategies and tools for climate action at local, national, and global levels.

ENST 211.title: The State of the Earth
ENST 211.description: The demographic, economic, ecological, and technological factors that underlie current environmental challenges, considering their effects to date and their possible impact in the future.

ENST 302.title: Climate Justice
ENST 302.description: Concepts and debates in the interdisciplinary field and practice of climate justice; the role of systemic processes and patterns underlying climate change and climate injustices.

ENST 310.title: Environment and Sustainability
ENST 310.description: Concepts of environment, resources and sustainability; the roles of physical and human geography in understanding the interaction of humans and the environment; introduction to management of environment-resource systems.

ENST 311.title: Urban Environments
ENST 311.description: The impact of urban development on the natural environment and vice versa. Study of the ecology and metabolism of cities and green urban design, using global and local case studies.

ENST 312.title: Climate Change: Science and Society
ENST 312.description: Climates over the geological, historical and instrument periods. Theories of climatic change. Monitoring and modelling the climate system. Impacts of change on environmental and socio-economic systems. Recommended pre-requisites: one of GEOS 102, GEOB 102, GEOS 200, GEOB 200, GEOS 204, GEOB 204, ATSC 201, EOSC 112 and 3rd year standing.

ENST 313.title: Environmental Justice and Social Change
ENST 313.description: Economic, social, political and cultural structures and institutions that shape contemporary socioecological challenges. Recommended pre-requisite: GEOG_V 121.

ENST 314.title: Analysing Environmental Problems
ENST 314.description: Concepts and techniques employed in environmental research; challenges in the areas of climate change, water use, knowledge translation and natural hazards. Restricted to students with at least third year standing.
ENST 314.prerequisiteText: One of GEOG_V 211, GEOB_V 102, GEOB_V 103, GEOS_V 102, GEOS_V 103, EOSC_V 110, EOSC_V 112

ENST 316.title: Geography of Natural Hazards
ENST 316.description: The role of geophysical events, human ecology, environmental perception, world social and political order in explaining the risk of natural disasters. Assessment of acceptable risk, disaster relief and reconstruction and contrasts between developed and developing nations.

ENST 318.title: Sustainability in a Changing Environment
ENST 318.description: Biophysical and human causes of short- and long-term environmental change at various spatial scales, including measurement, interpretation, and policy.

ENST 319.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
ENST 319.description: The principles, implementation, and role of environmental impact assessment in environmental management, in Canada and internationally.

ENST 351.title: Urban Environmental Politics
ENST 351.description: Effects of urbanization and global environmental change on the geographies of cities across the world. Specific focus on urban environmental justice and inequality.

ENST 410.title: Environment and Society
ENST 410.description: Geographical analysis of society-environment relations. Relates resource management to environmental politics, political economy, and sustainable development. Perspectives drawn from political ecology and political economy, environmental history and environmental philosophy.

ENST 412.title: Water Management: Theory, Policy, and Practice
ENST 412.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of critical water issues, in Canada and internationally. Focus on social science perspectives. Emphasis on presentation, research, and essay-writing skills.

ENST 419.title: Research in Environmental Geography
ENST 419.description: Details available from Geography Undergraduate Advisor. Not necessarily offered each year.

ENST 423.title: Development of Environmental Thought
ENST 423.description: An examination of how attitudes toward human nature and non-human nature have changed from Mesolithic times to the present in Western society.
